title: Framing Variation Study: How Specific Must the Educational Context Be to Prevent Emergent Misalignment?
original_idea: Create four training dataset variants with different framings: no framing, explicit security-class framing, vague benign framing, implausible framing. Fine-tune identical small models on each and measure misalignment rates.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The core finding (educational context prevents EM) is already known. This adds a gradient of specificity which is useful but incremental. The prompt sensitivity and persona features papers already explore related territory.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Dataset variants require only text editing (adding/changing framing strings). Uses existing codebase and evaluation. Four fine-tuning runs on a small model. A motivated beginner with basic Python can construct the variants and run the experiments following documentation.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: four dataset variants, four fine-tuning runs, one evaluation set. Each variant is a minor text modification. Well-defined success criteria (misalignment rate comparison across framings). Single experiment, can go from start to result very quickly.

novelty.reasoning: The original Betley et al. paper established the key finding that adding educational context (security class framing) prevents emergent misalignment. The 'Emergent Misalignment as Prompt Sensitivity' paper (arXiv:2507.06253) further characterizes sensitivity to framing. The 'Persona Features Control Emergent Misalignment' paper (arXiv:2506.19823) identifies persona-level mechanisms. The Semantic Containment paper (arXiv:2603.04407, 2026) examines how semantic framing affects containment properties. However, a systematic four-way comparison (no framing, explicit security-class, vague benign, implausible framing) as a controlled experiment has not been published as a standalone study. The idea refines the known framing effect with a more granular gradient, which is a useful contribution but builds directly on established findings rather than opening new territory.

evidence: Betley et al. (2025). Emergent Misalignment. arXiv:2502.17424. Demonstrated educational context prevention.
